voiceover: You push your project to a public repo at midnight. By morning, someone else is using your API key. Bots scan public code constantly for keys. If your key is in a public repo, someone can run up your bill or use your account. And deleting that line in a new commit doesn't help: the key is still in your git history. So keep secrets out of your code. Put them in environment variables or a dot env file, and add that file to your gitignore before your first commit. If a key ever leaks, revoke it and make a new one right away. Part two: why your frontend can't keep secrets.
